commands.review_summary:
The PR defers initial ACP session snapshot and available-command notifications until after `newSession` and `resumeSession` return their JSON-RPC results, adding lifecycle and NDJSON ordering tests.

PR surface: Source +12, Tests +585. Total +597 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: current `main` awaits `session_info_update` before returning in both lifecycle handlers. The reported Rabbit-specific hang was not independently reproduced in a real client setup.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A narrow mechanical repair can make the deferred lifecycle work safe; contributor-supplied real ACP proof remains a separate human merge gate.

target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`newSession()` and `resumeSession()` in the ACP bridge send the `session_info_update` notification via `sendSessionSnapshotUpdate` BEFORE returning the JSON-RPC result. Clients that key off `session_info_update` to learn the sessionId receive a notification referencing a sessionId they have not yet parsed from the result.

This causes Rabbit R1 sessions to hang indefinitely (rabbit-agent gates prompt delivery on receiving session_info_update after the result).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix defers the notification and subsequent `sendAvailableCommands` to fire asynchronously after the result is returned, using `setTimeout(..., 0)` to cross the response-write boundary. Both `newSession()` (line 394) and `resumeSession()` (line 554) are fixed. The full promise chain has a terminal `.catch()` handler.

## User Impact

Clients that expect session_info_update after the session/new or resume result now receive correct ordering. No change to the API contract, response shape, or notification content.

## Evidence

### Ordering tests (transport-level)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```
Two new tests verify that `session_info_update` is NOT called before the lifecycle handler resolves, and IS called after flushing timers — confirming result-before-notification ordering at the transport boundary.

### All ACP tests
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

### Typecheck
```
pnpm tsgo:core — EXIT: 0
```

### Fix pattern
Before: `await sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...)` → `return { sessionId, ... }`
After:  `return { sessionId, ... }` → `setTimeout(() => sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...).then(...).catch(...), 0)`
